title: How the Capstone Video Agent Works
topic: How the capstone-video-agent repository turns a text prompt into a narrated, fact-checked MP4 through a chain of specialised AI agents, and why it is designed that way.
audience: Technically curious viewers, such as business or data students and AI practitioners, who know what an LLM is but have not seen multi-agent pipelines or this repository.
angle: Whether splitting video creation into specialised agents that hand off files (research, script, fact-check, audio-first build) makes the output more reliable than one prompt, and where each stage earns its place.
tone: clear and neutral, like a business-school explainer

key_questions.question: According to README.md, CLAUDE.md and .claude/skills/make-video/SKILL.md, what are the pipeline stages in order (intake, parallel researchers, scriptwriter, length fit, fact-checker, voiceover, parallel scene-builders, render and stitch), what does each produce, and which run in parallel?
key_questions.why: Scene 1: the walkthrough of the pipeline from prompt to finished video.

key_questions.question: How do stages hand off work through files in runs/<slug>/ (brief.json, research/<qid>.json, scenes.json, factcheck.json, vo.wav, renders, final mp4), and what does scenes.json contain?
key_questions.why: Scene 1: shows the file-based hand-off design that connects the agents.

key_questions.question: How do the scriptwriter and length-fit steps in .claude/agents/ and docs/ keep narration within the target duration and tie each sentence to cited fact ids in claims?
key_questions.why: Scene 1 and 2: links script quality and length control to the design.

key_questions.question: What does the fact-checker agent verify and what rule decides which narration reaches the voiceover (only claims marked supported)?
key_questions.why: Scene 2: explains why the pipeline is built for trustworthiness.

key_questions.question: Why does the pipeline generate audio first and time visuals to the measured audio (the timing block), and how do parallel scene-builders render standalone HyperFrames scenes before stitching?
key_questions.why: Scene 2: explains the audio-first and parallel build design rationale.

key_questions.question: What reasons do README.md and docs/ give for the multi-agent design (specialised agents, parallelism, file hand-offs, run_log.json), and what limits or trade-offs do they note?

must_include: Explanation of the pipeline stages: intake, parallel researchers, scriptwriter, length fit, fact-checker, voiceover, parallel scene-builders, render and stitch
Why the project is built this way
Primary sources are the repository files: README.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/agents/*.md, .claude/skills/make-video, docs/
out_of_scope: Installation, environment setup and tools/env.sh details
Per-agent prompt wording and code-level implementation
HyperFrames style guide and visual design details
The prototypes/ folder and Step 1 experiments
Capstone sponsor and course background beyond a passing mention
assumptions: The prompt's own repository files are the primary sources, so research reads local files rather than the public web; public sources are only for brief background such as HyperFrames or Kokoro TTS.
At 60 seconds and 2 scenes, scene 1 covers what the pipeline does (stage-by-stage) and scene 2 covers why it is built that way (fact-checking, audio-first timing, parallelism).
The audience is general technical learners, not the capstone sponsors.
Length fit and the other stages are described as they appear in the repository, even if some are folded into the same agent.
